inconsistencies: Three PRs solve the same trace-logging configuration problem: #34038 (-trace + RPC), #35387 (standalone -loglevel + loglevel RPC) and #35355 (-trace + atomics + RPC). Review #34038 first and treat the others as alternatives; merging more than one would duplicate work.
#35322 and #35355 both replace the Logger's mutex-guarded level map with atomic bitmasks. Whichever is reviewed first makes the other largely redundant; #35322 is the narrower of the two.
Args chain, order matters: #16545 -> #17580 -> {#17783, #17493 -> #17581}. #17493 and #17581 are user-facing/cleanup leaves that cannot be evaluated before the base flags land.
util::Result chain: #25665 -> #26022 -> #25722, and #25665 -> #29700. #25665 is the only one worth reviewing until it settles.
Logging chain: #34778 -> #29256 -> #30342 -> #30343. #34778 carries an unresolved Concept NACK on macro design; that decision gates the entire stack, which is why it is banded with its dependents.
#36190 only tests behaviour introduced by #36105; review #36105 first.
#19461 is a single commit on top of #19460 (and the multiprocess branch); reviewing it standalone is not meaningful.
#36295 (remove args wrappers) exists to simplify #31260; it is marginal on its own but should be looked at alongside #31260 rather than in isolation.
Silent payments: #36338 fixes pubkey extraction in BIP352 code that #32966 and #35302 build on, so it should be reviewed before either feature PR.
#26966 (parallel index sync thread pool) is described as proceeding alongside #34489; check the two are not duplicating the same threading utility.
result.notes: Only two PRs meet the P1 bar here: silent block-file corruption on reindex (#35524) and missed silent-payment funds (#36338). The P2 band is large but genuinely stratified: crash/memory-safety/regression fixes in shared primitives first (#36049, #35281, #35744, #35422, #36340), then security and user-facing config/CLI fixes, then the argument- and error-handling infrastructure whose value is mostly through dependents, then measured performance work. Two band changes: #26966 up to P2 (biggest measured speedup plus a reusable threading primitive) and #34778 up to P2 (prerequisite for a P2 dependent). Much of the P3 mass is one author's stacked refactors plus three overlapping logging proposals; ordering there follows the chains rather than individual merit.
